identity.name: Starch sodium octenyl succinate
identity.chemical_class: Chemically modified starch (starch ester; OSA-modified starch)

function.mechanism: Esterification of starch with octenyl succinic groups creates an amphiphilic modified starch that stabilizes oil-water interfaces and improves emulsion stability/texture.
common_food_categories: special infant medical formulas and related infant nutrition uses
processed foods using modified starch as emulsifier/stabilizer

adi.basis: EFSA FAF (2020) reiterated the ANS conclusion that there is no need for a numerical ADI for E1450/modified starch context.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no indication for safety concern for infants below 16 weeks within the clinical-study exposure range (up to 2,725 mg/kg bw/day), while noting important data-quality limitations.

fda.notes: Handled under food additive rules for modified starch (not as a standalone GRAS affirmation in retrieved CFR context); retrieved CFR text includes OSA treatment limits (e.g., up to 3% in specified modification pathway) and beverage-related use constraints including a retrieved additive-specific page showing up to 0.2% in finished beverages.

adi.basis: JECFA INS 1450 record lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED in toxicological evaluations; latest listed year (2018) is specification-only.

concerns.summary: EFSA 2020 found infant clinical evidence had mostly high risk of bias and could not derive a formal reference point; uncertainty remained despite lack of clear adverse signal.
EFSA noted that some estimated infant exposures (especially high-end/MPL scenarios in FSMP) may exceed the upper clinical-study exposure range used for no-concern interpretation.
EFSA discussed microbiome-related considerations in infants but concluded that microbiome composition shifts alone are difficult to interpret without specific health outcomes.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 and 2020 opinions did not identify a clear safety concern at evaluated use levels and retained non-numerical ADI framing.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for INS 1450 and retained this across later evaluations.
A neonatal piglet dietary study (2014) reported no treatment-related adverse effects at tested concentrations.

populations: Infants below 16 weeks consuming foods for special medical purposes at high-end or maximum permitted use scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: There is no numerical ADI; however EFSA indicated that modeled high exposures can exceed the upper clinical-study exposure range (about 2,725 mg/kg bw/day) used in its no-concern interpretation.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus (EFSA/JECFA/FDA-CFR) remains permissive with no numerical ADI, no clear adverse-effect signal, and no IARC carcinogenic classification for this additive. The main caveat is uncertainty in infant datasets and potential high-end infant exposures above the clinical evidence range.
key_factors: EFSA 2020 follow-up for infants found no indication for safety concern within studied exposure range
EFSA 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern at reported uses
FDA/eCFR places the substance under 21 CFR 172.892 food additive controls
Infant high-end exposure uncertainty remains the main residual risk driver
